# sorting.library: Sort

**Status:** Supported (tier `foundation`). In a shipping tier; the lint, type-check, and code-generation gates cover it. No release promises its signature yet.

## Summary

> A new array holding the elements of `xs` in ascending `lessOrEqual`
> order. Stable, as SortedIndices is. When positions matter — attributes
> to carry along, source indices to report — use SortedIndices instead.

## Signature

```plato
Sort(xs: Array<$T>, lessOrEqual: Function2<$T, $T, Boolean>): Array<$T>
```

## Laws

These are declared laws. Whether each one passes is recorded by the law runner ([stdlib/VERIFICATION.md](../../../../../stdlib/VERIFICATION.md)), not by this page.

### Law_SortOrdersAdjacentPairs

[stdlib/tests/sorting.laws.plato, line 17](../../../../../stdlib/tests/sorting.laws.plato#L17)

```plato
// Sorting orders the elements: every adjacent pair of the output is in
// ascending order.
Law_SortOrdersAdjacentPairs(xs: Array<Number>): Boolean
    => xs.Sort((a, b) => a <= b).AdjacentPairsAscend;
```

### Law_SortPreservesCount

[stdlib/tests/sorting.laws.plato, line 21](../../../../../stdlib/tests/sorting.laws.plato#L21)

```plato
// Sorting neither invents nor drops elements.
Law_SortPreservesCount(xs: Array<Number>): Boolean
    => xs.Sort((a, b) => a <= b).Count == xs.Count;
```

    // A new array holding the elements of `xs` in ascending `lessOrEqual`
